claim: The decision problem α-Subgraph-Balanced-Vertex-Separator is NP-complete, and the underlying optimization/search problem is NP-hard, even when the constructed graph instances are exactly 3-regular.
falsifier: The classification can be challenged by checking the reduction for correctness: verify that every Yes instance of α-Subgraph-Balanced-Vertex-Separator maps to a Yes instance of α-Balanced-Vertex-Separator and that the constructed graphs are exactly 3-regular.

conditions: the separator is required to satisfy the α-subgraph-balanced vertex separator condition
the decision variant asks whether such a separator exists
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported reduction construction and the formal proof supplied; transfer of the hardness classification to other graph classes or parameter regimes is unestablished.

title: Graph partitioning decision problems–NP-hardness of the problem theorem
